title: Region Evacuation Coordinator and Passive Standby Health Validator
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build a coordinator service and validation harness that orchestrates planned or emergency region evacuation while ensuring passive warm standby readiness. The coordinator must sequence capacity gating, drain policies, and traffic reroute with an independent validator that performs non-invasive health checks against standby fleets: KV/cache priming checks, model artifact availability, kernel compatibility probes, and latency envelope probes. The goal is to reduce user-facing errors and tail latency during cutover and avoid large cold-start spikes by detecting unhealthy standby nodes before traffic is routed. This ticket covers design, implementation, test harness, and a staged rollout to staging and alpha Dedicated clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator can initiate an evacuation runbook and produce deterministic steps (quiesce ingress, shadow prefetch, route update, final cutover)
Validator reports per-standby readiness score (0-100) and a boolean 'traffic-safe' flag using non-invasive probes
During simulated cutover with 10% shadow traffic, median added latency <= 15ms and 95th percentile increase <= 60ms across requests routed to standby
When validator flags a standby as unsafe, coordinator must automatically select an alternative region or fallback model variant without dropping active requests
Runbook execution logs and metrics are visible in Console (run id, step durations, health scores) and a post-run artifact is stored in Confluence
design_decisions: Use a centralized coordinator with pluggable policy modules (latency-first, cost-first, compliance-first) to decide evacuation target
Validator performs passive probes only (shadowed inference + lightweight synthetic traces) to avoid polluting production cache state; active prefetch is an opt-in policy
Standby readiness computed from weighted signals: model artifact present (40%), KV cache hit estimate (25%), kernel compatibility test (15%), p95 latency probe (20%)

Fallback model variants are declared in the model catalog with compatibility labels. Coordinator will prefer same-architecture quantized variants before falling back to smaller/cheaper but semantically-similar models
All decision steps are auditable and reversible; every route change must be accompanied by an automated rollback predicate triggered by error budget breaches or spike in 5xxs
tradeoffs: Passive shadow probing reduces cache pollution but delays detection of certain runtime failures compared to active prefetching
Keeping warm standby capacity >20% increases cost but materially reduces cold-start risk; we default to conservative capacity for high-SLA customers only
Aggressive automatic fallback to smaller variants reduces latency but may degrade output quality; we surface quality regressions to console and tie behavior to customer tier
Centralized coordinator simplifies orchestration but is a single control-plane dependency; mitigations include a highly-available deployment and local failover policies
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime, and Console teams. Agreed API for coordinator -> region-agent is a lightweight gRPC command stream
2026-02-18: Prototype validator implemented that runs p95 latency probes and artifact presence checks against staging; initial readiness scoring introduced
2026-02-25: Discovered race when updating routing table and concurrent autoscaler scales up standby nodes; added preflight quiesce signal to autoscaler (PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/3410)

2026-03-02: Load test with synthetic region outage: warm hit-rate improved from 3% to 72% when shadow prefetch enabled; observed transient 5xx spike during final cutover—investigating drain timeout tuning
2026-03-06: Design review feedback from PM (Priya Desai) to expose fallback variant quality thresholds in Console. Action: add UI knobs and telemetry mapping

2026-03-10: E2E staging rollout to alpha cluster completed behind feature flag region_evacuate_v2. Canary run id: run-20260310-07. No major customer-impacting errors observed. Next: expand to two additional regions and schedule DR drill
